The Arbaeen Walk — Najaf to Karbala

The road walked by millions each year for the Arbaeen of Imam Hussain (a.s.) — traced here with its numbered poles, so you always know how far you have come and how far remains.

80 km
Distance
~3
Days on foot
1,452
Numbered poles
20M+
Walkers each year

The walk begins at the shrine of Imam Ali (a.s.) in Najaf and ends some 80 kilometres north at the shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.) in Karbala. Most walkers take about three days, resting at night and walking in the cool of the morning and evening.

The route is lined with 1,452 numbered poles, roughly 50 metres apart. The pole numbers are the walk's own address system: families agree a pole number to meet at, walkers tell each other where they stopped, and help can be directed to an exact spot. All along the road, mawakib — volunteer stalls run by families, towns and organisations — offer free food, water, tea, places to rest and medical help to every passer-by, asking nothing in return.

Walking tips

  • Start before dawn and rest through the midday heat; the road is kindest in the early hours.
  • Carry a light bag only — food, water and rest are provided at mawakib all along the way.
  • Fix a pole number as your group's meeting point in case you get separated in the crowd.
  • Wear shoes you have already broken in, and carry a small power bank for your phone.
  • Note the pole numbers where you sleep, so you can rejoin the road exactly where you left it.

Made in service of the zaireen

Every year, millions of pilgrims travel to Iraq and Iran to visit the shrines of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) — many of them for the first time, in a country whose language they may not speak. Ziyarat Maps exists so that no pilgrim feels lost on that journey: every sacred place, gathered on one clear map, with honest directions and the great Arbaeen road explained pole by pole.

The project begins with Iraq — Najaf, Kufa, Karbala, Baghdad and Samarra — and will grow, God willing, to Mashhad, Qom and beyond. If it helps even one pilgrim reach a shrine with a little less worry, it has done its work.

May every step of every zaireen be accepted.
